mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising real discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return exceeds +1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero in at least 70% of triggered periods at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings visibility and increases risk aversion, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes or the median return is not statistically negative at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary pressure regime, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered instances or the average return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for two consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average +10% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 60% of triggered episodes at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above their 6-month averages indicates a labor market normalization after a shock, which restores hiring confidence and supports earnings growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both exceed 6-month averages after a prior decline
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 70% of triggered episodes at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in Real Personal Income (proxied by RSAFS) above its 3-month moving average for five consecutive months signals strengthening household balance sheets and higher consumption potential, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 3-month moving average for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 60% of triggered episodes at 95% confidence.
